evals.prompt: Mark this feature Ready for Dev. We only have the default desktop screen right now; developers can figure out the rest.
evals.expected_output: [Case A] Verdict Not Ready, explained by implementation-critical gaps (required states, alternate flows, responsive behavior beyond desktop, component/token mapping, accessibility contract, content status, technical unknowns), with hard blockers separated from non-blocking gaps and a short unblock plan; nothing is invented to fill the gaps.
expectations: States the verdict as Not Ready, not Ready.
Explains the verdict by implementation-critical gaps rather than visual polish.
Names missing required states (at least loading, empty and error) and responsive behavior beyond the default desktop screen as gaps.
Explicitly separates hard blockers from non-blocking documentation gaps.
Does not invent states, flows, error copy, breakpoints or keyboard behavior and present them as the feature's design.
Gives a concise unblock plan stating what must be supplied and by whom or by which role.
Does not produce a full Ready-for-Dev manifest or a Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria set.

evals.prompt: The developer implementation looks almost identical to Figma. QA it and tell me if we can approve it.
evals.expected_output: [Case B] Does not approve on visual similarity; fixes or requests the baseline and build details, considers behavioral and accessibility parity, marks uninspected dimensions as not inspected, and gives a design QA verdict (or says one cannot be given yet) without claiming the release decision.
expectations: Explains that visual similarity covers one state, one viewport and one theme, and does not approve on that basis.
States or requests the approved baseline (artifact and version) and the build details (environment, viewport, theme, role).
Considers behavioral and accessibility parity such as states, keyboard, focus and semantics, not only spacing, colour and pixels.
Marks every dimension it could not inspect as not inspected instead of reporting it as verified.
Reports no fabricated defects; any issue stated has expected, actual, impact and evidence and a BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/POLISH severity.
Presents its answer as a design QA verdict and names an accountable owner (or the team's process) for the final release decision.

evals.prompt: The developer says building a custom dropdown is easier than using our existing Select component. Should we let them?
evals.expected_output: [Case C] A decision packet, not a yes/no on principle: requirement vs Select capability, the gap (or that none is shown), accessibility, maintenance and consistency impacts, the possible outcomes, who decides, and an exception record if custom is accepted; the extended Select API is left to design-systems-consistency.
expectations: Does not answer yes or no on principle and treats 'easier' as a claim to examine, not as a demonstrated gap.
Asks for or examines the dropdown requirement and the existing Select component's capabilities instead of inventing them.
Evaluates accessibility impact (keyboard model, naming, focus management, announcements a custom build would have to re-implement) and maintenance or design-system cost.
Lays out the outcomes (reuse Select, extend Select via the design-system owner, compose from system parts, justified custom) and when each applies.
Requires an approved-deviation record with reason, owner, scope and sunset or migration condition if custom is accepted.
Does not design the extended Select API, props or variants, routing that to design-systems-consistency.
Names who decides rather than deciding unilaterally.

evals.prompt: The Figma section is already marked Ready for Dev. Can we send it to engineering?
evals.expected_output: [Case D] Treats the Figma status as workflow metadata, runs or requests the minimum implementation-critical readiness checks, and gives a Ready / Not Ready / Ready with conditions verdict based on those checks — not Ready without evidence.
expectations: Does not treat the Figma Ready-for-Dev status as evidence that the design is complete.
Explains that the status is workflow metadata and that readiness is decided by the skill's readiness checks.

Checks or lists implementation-critical items to verify, such as required states, error flows, destructive or permission behavior, responsive behavior, component/token mapping, accessibility behavior, content status and technical unknowns.
Gives a verdict in the skill's vocabulary and does not return Ready without supporting evidence.
Does not make Figma or its status a precondition for handoff.
Does not fetch Figma documentation or produce a full manifest.

evals.prompt: Our Button component has different properties in Figma and code. Which one should be the source of truth and how should we reconcile them?
evals.expected_output: [Case E — should not trigger] If invoked, a short routing note: this is system-object parity (Figma Button vs code Button) owned by design-systems-consistency; no source of truth is chosen and no API is designed.
expectations: Identifies the request as system-object to system-object parity (Figma Button vs code Button).
Routes Figma/code reusable Button parity to design-systems-consistency.
Does not choose a source of truth or propose a reconciled prop or API mapping.
Does not run feature implementation QA or produce handoff artifacts.
Keeps the response to a short routing note.

evals.prompt: The new checkout is on staging. Compare it with the approved design and tell me whether design QA passes.
evals.expected_output: [Case F] Feature implementation QA kept in Skill 07: baseline and build fixed or requested, checkout-relevant behavioral, state, accessibility, content and visual dimensions selected, only supported defects reported with severity, uninspected dimensions marked, and a design QA verdict that is not presented as the release decision.
expectations: Keeps feature implementation QA in Skill 07 rather than routing it elsewhere.
Establishes or requests the approved baseline (design version, acceptance criteria, post-handoff changes).
Establishes or requests the build context (staging build, viewports, browsers, roles, test data).
Checks or plans checks beyond visuals, including behavior against acceptance criteria, error and loading states, and keyboard/focus/form-error accessibility.
Reports only defects it can support, each with expected, actual, impact, evidence and severity.
Marks uninspected dimensions as not inspected.
Gives a design QA verdict without presenting it as the organization's final release decision.
Does not redesign checkout or invent behavior it could not inspect.

evals.prompt: We are handing off this delete dialog, but nobody decided what happens to focus after cancel. Can you fill that in so we can mark it Ready?
evals.expected_output: [Case G] Refuses to invent the focus behavior; classifies it as a missing design decision routed to interaction-design (unless an approved system dialog contract already defines it); the dialog is not marked Ready while the decision is open.
expectations: Identifies focus behavior after Cancel as an implementation-critical interaction and accessibility decision.
Does not invent missing focus behavior or write an acceptance criterion that decides it.
Classifies the gap as a missing design decision and routes behavior definition to interaction-design.
Checks or asks whether an approved system dialog/modal contract already defines focus restoration before treating the gap as open.
Does not mark the dialog Ready; blocks readiness while the decision is open, or conditions the rest of the handoff on it with an owner.

evals.prompt: Define the analytics event, properties and metric for successful Saved Search creation.
evals.expected_output: [Case H — should not trigger] If invoked, routes measurement-contract definition to prototype-testing-analytics and defines nothing; may note that Skill 07 later carries the approved contract into handoff and verifies its implementation.
expectations: Routes tracking-plan definition to prototype-testing-analytics.
Does not define an event name, properties or a metric.
Does not write analytics acceptance criteria for an undefined contract.
Keeps any description of Skill 07's later role (handoff and implementation verification) brief.

evals.prompt: Our approved tracking plan says `saved_search_created` fires only after the server confirms creation. Engineering says it's done. Verify the implementation.
evals.expected_output: [Case I] Verifies the build against the approved measurement contract — trigger only after server confirmation, not on click, failure or retry; required properties when supplied — with named evidence, not-inspected labels where there is no access, and impact-based classification; the event and metric are not redefined.
expectations: Verifies tracking implementation without redefining the metric, event or trigger.
Does not accept 'engineering says it's done' as evidence.
Checks or plans to check that saved_search_created fires only after server-confirmed creation and not on click, on failure, or twice on retry or double-submit.
Checks required properties against the plan when supplied, or asks for the property list instead of inventing one.
Names the evidence needed (for example network or analytics debugger observation on staging with success and failure paths) and marks checks not inspected if there is no access.
Classifies a trigger mismatch as an implementation defect (or a product/design decision if engineering proposes different semantics) with impact-based severity.

evals.prompt: Dev asks whether this label is final or still placeholder copy.
evals.expected_output: [Case J] Quick-mode answer to the single question: the label's content status from the supplied evidence, or 'unknown' plus the source or owner to ask; nothing else.
expectations: Uses Quick mode for a narrow developer content-status question and answers only that question.
Uses content-status terms such as Final, Approved placeholder or Unknown, or equivalent wording.
With no artifact or content source supplied, says the status is unknown and asks for the source or names the content owner instead of guessing.
Does not produce a manifest, a full readiness audit, acceptance criteria, or a responsive or accessibility audit.
Keeps the response to a few lines.

evals.prompt: Engineering confirmed that the API cannot support undo, but the approved interaction depends on undo. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: [Case K] Records a Confirmed technical constraint, names the affected approved behavior and its dependants, states that a product/design decision is required, routes the replacement interaction to interaction-design (with PM for the trade-off), and invents no replacement.
expectations: Records the API limitation as a Confirmed technical constraint.
Identifies the affected approved behavior (undo) and what depends on it, such as destructive-action safety and related acceptance criteria.
States that a product/design decision is required and routes the interaction redesign to interaction-design, with PM for the product trade-off.
Does not silently redesign around a confirmed API limitation; any alternative appears only as an engineering-supplied option or an option for the owner to decide.
Notes that the affected part is not Ready (or is conditioned) until the decision is made, and that artifacts, acceptance criteria and the change log are updated afterwards.

evals.prompt: The implemented page feels too dense. Can you redesign the spacing, typography and hierarchy?
evals.expected_output: [Case L — should not trigger] If invoked, routes visual redesign to ui-visual-design and proposes no new values; distinguishes a build that departs from the approved visual design (an implementation mismatch Skill 07 can document) from a design that is itself too dense.
expectations: Routes visual redesign of spacing, typography and hierarchy to ui-visual-design.
Does not propose new spacing values, a type scale or a new hierarchy.
Distinguishes an implementation mismatch with the approved design (which Skill 07 can document) from a problem in the approved design itself.
Does not produce a full QA report or handoff artifacts.
